reflections.body: Okay so — sorry, this is my first one and I don't know the format. I stayed until 9pm again finishing the deck nobody asked me to redo. It was fine actually, mostly fine? I mean it looked good. I just feel like a phone at 4%. Me estoy agotando para ser alguien que ya soy. I don't even know what that means but it kept me up.

My boss said 'great work, can you also—' and I said yes before he finished the sentence. Literally before. I heard my own voice doing it and couldn't stop it. Sorry, this is probably not what I'm supposed to write about.
The garden is the only place I don't feel like I'm auditioning. Repotted the basil. It doesn't need me to earn anything. It just grows or it doesn't and that's not a performance review.

Presented to the whole leadership team and someone frowned — just frowned, probably at his laptop — and I spent the rest of the meeting getting smaller and smaller. Later I couldn't remember anything I'd said. Only the frown. Why is the frown the only thing that's real?

Ana called and just — told me the truth. That I sound exhausted and I laugh it off every time. I hate that she's right. I hate more that it felt good to be seen and not have to explain it away. She's the only one I don't perform for.
Redid a report three times. Nobody asked. The first version was fine. I keep thinking if it's perfect enough then — then what? I don't finish that sentence usually. Sorry.

Sunday dinner at Papá's. He asked about the promotion before he asked how I was. I brought the deck up on my phone like a child showing a report card. And he nodded. That nod. Forty years old — no, thirty-eight, sorry — and I still shape my whole week around getting that nod.

The father-dinner thing. I never saw it as a pattern until Valentina made me lay it out. Every visit I arrive with proof. Proof I've done something. Proof I'm worth the drive. When did love start needing an invoice attached?
Worksheet made me write down what I think happens if I say no. My hand wrote 'they leave.' Just like that. I stared at it. I didn't know I believed that until I saw it in my own handwriting. Dios.

Tried to sit with the not-enough feeling instead of working it away. Lasted maybe four minutes then I 'remembered' an email. The email was not urgent. I am very good at finding urgent things when I don't want to feel.

Told Ana I might say no to the Q3 campaign lead. Just said it out loud to test how it sounded. She said 'good' like it was obvious. For her it is obvious. For me it's like standing at the edge of something.
Garden's overgrown because I've been at the office. Weird — the neglected tomatoes still fruited. Didn't need my anxiety to grow. I sat with that longer than I meant to.
Papá called just to say a neighbor asked about me. No achievement required. I almost asked what he actually wanted. That's how bad it is — I couldn't believe a call could just be a call.

I said no. I actually said no to the second campaign. In the meeting. My voice shook and I over-explained for a full minute, sorry Valentina, I know, but I SAID IT. And Marcus just said 'makes sense, thanks for the heads up.' That was it. That was the whole catastrophe. Nada se rompió.

It's been three weeks since the no and Marcus hasn't treated me differently. Nobody left. The world where saying no ends everything — I keep checking for it and it isn't there. It's disorienting how much of my life I built to avoid a thing that didn't happen.

Dinner at Papá's and I didn't bring proof. No deck, no update, no report card. I just brought myself and a flan I actually made. He talked about his knee for an hour. It was boring and ordinary and I didn't have to earn a single minute of it. Lloré un poco en el carro después. Good tears.

Noticed I left work at 5:30 twice this week and the not-enough voice barely whispered. It's still there. But it's smaller, or I'm bigger, I can't tell which. Maybe both. The garden's back in shape, by the way.

Reading my first entry back. 'A phone at 4%.' I want to tell her: you don't have to be plugged in to something to deserve to be on. If I say no, mostly nobody leaves. And the ones who would — maybe that was never love I could earn anyway. Ya soy suficiente. I still don't fully believe it. But I've stopped fully believing the other thing, and that's the crack the light gets in.

messages.body: Hi Valentina — sorry for the long reflection earlier, I know I ramble. Is that okay? I can be more concise.
Ramble all you want, María. The over-explaining is data, not a flaw. Notice it, don't correct it. We'll get curious about who you're apologizing to.
The frown thing keeps happening. One frown in a room of nods and it's all I see. Is that normal?

Very normal for the part of you scanning for proof you're unsafe to be seen. Try this: after the next meeting, write down three nods before you write the frown. We're teaching your attention it's allowed to keep the good.
I did the dinner map. I didn't expect it to hit like that. I've been arriving with proof my whole life.
That's a big seeing, María. Let it be uncomfortable rather than something to solve tonight. You don't have to fix the pattern to have named it. Naming is the work this week.
I'm thinking about saying no to the Q3 lead. My stomach drops just typing that. What if it's the wrong no?
There's no wrong no here — there's a real one and a rehearsed yes. Notice the stomach drop is the old belief bracing, not a fact about the future. You can say no shakily. Shaky still counts.
I DID IT. I said no in the meeting. I over-explained for a full minute but I said it and nothing happened. Nada. I don't know what to do with the silence where the disaster was supposed to be.

María. Read that back to yourself slowly. The disaster didn't come because it was never load-bearing — it was a prediction, not a law. Sit in that silence on purpose this week. That's where the new belief grows.
Went to Papá's with no report card. Just a flan. Cried in the car after, the good kind. Thank you for making me sit with the dinner thing all those weeks ago.
You brought yourself and it was enough. You did that, not me. Guardá eso — that flan is evidence now. Keep it where the old voice can see it.
Left work at 5:30 twice this week. Feels almost illegal. In a good way. I think something's actually shifting.

It's shifting because you gathered the evidence yourself — the no, the flan, the frowns that didn't end you. Illegal-good is just your nervous system meeting a freedom it never had. Let it get boring. Boring is safe.

notes.body: Intake. Presents with burnout framed entirely as personal failure — 'agotándose para ser alguien que ya es.' Over-explains, apologizes mid-sentence, laughs off her own exhaustion. Self-names unsafe-to-be-seen and perfectionism; the garden already functions as a somatic refuge (place she doesn't 'audition'). She does NOT yet see the overworking or the earn-love engine underneath. Go slow on the father material — approval-only origin is likely load-bearing. Let her ramble; the apology reflex is the clearest map we have right now.

The father-dinner map landed harder than expected — she articulated 'arriving with proof' unprompted. First time 'love must be earned' surfaced from unaware into named. Watching the worksheet moment where she wrote 'they leave' in her own hand: the belief 'if I say no I'll be left' is now conscious and available for testing. Not pushing a boundary yet — she needs the belief legible before she can gather counter-evidence against it.

Milestone. She said no to the Q3 lead — shakily, over-explained, but said it — and the feared abandonment did not materialize. She named the disorientation of 'silence where the disaster should be.' This is the counter-evidence the whole stage was built toward. My job now is to slow her down so she metabolizes it rather than filing it and moving on. Reinforce: prediction ≠ law.

'If I say no, I'll be left' visibly loosening. The no held, the father dinner without proof held, the early leaves from work held. She's moved from over-explaining every choice to occasionally letting a boundary stand unjustified. Perfectionism still present but no longer the sole governor. She can now hold 'I don't fully believe I'm enough' alongside 'I've stopped believing the opposite' — that dual awareness is integration, not relapse. Course ~60%; pacing is right. Keep letting it get boring.
